result:
If I could change the world in one way, I’d make a rigorous, humane education universal and lifelong—one that teaches people how to think, not what to think; how to weigh evidence; how to hold uncertainty; and how to imagine the lives of others.

Not because education alone fixes everything, but because most other changes—better governance, less violence, wiser technology, climate action, less poverty—depend on enough people being able to reason clearly, resist manipulation, and care about consequences beyond themselves. It’s the closest thing to a root-level upgrade for humanity.
